figures.caption: Fig. 1. (a) We use a wrist-mounted force-torque (FT) sensor to sense human-object contact. (b) Example human-object contacts during robot-tohuman handovers: firm grasps on the left, where the robot can safely release the object, and incidental touches on the right, where premature release risks dropping the object. Across diverse rigid objects and grasp behaviors, our active sensing approach reliably distinguishes between them, while passive methods often fail.
Fig. 4. We selected 30 types of objects from the YCB dataset [7] and a human study [8]. These objects span a broad range of shapes and weights.
